statement: Phương trình vi phân thường (ODE) là quan hệ giữa một hàm chưa biết của một biến độc lập và các đạo hàm thường của hàm đó; bậc của ODE là bậc đạo hàm cao nhất thực sự xuất hiện.
scope_limits: ODE definition; derivative primitive remains C05-owned.

statement: Bài toán giá trị đầu x'(t)=f(t,x(t)), x(t0)=x0 có nghiệm trên khoảng I chứa t0 khi x khả vi, nhận giá trị trong miền của f, thỏa phương trình trên I và thỏa điều kiện đầu.
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional first-order IVP; writing data alone does not imply existence.

statement: Nếu f liên tục gần (t0,x0) và locally Lipschitz theo x ở đó, thì x'=f(t,x), x(t0)=x0 có một nghiệm địa phương duy nhất quanh t0.
scope_limits: Picard–Lindelöf; conclusion is local and the state-Lipschitz hypothesis supplies uniqueness.

statement: Nếu f chỉ liên tục gần (t0,x0), Peano-type existence bảo đảm ít nhất một nghiệm địa phương trong hữu hạn chiều nhưng không bảo đảm uniqueness.
scope_limits: Local existence under continuity; uniqueness needs additional hypotheses.

statement: Local existence và uniqueness không tự suy ra global existence: maximal solution có thể chỉ tồn tại trên khoảng hữu hạn nếu trạng thái rời miền vector field hoặc trở nên không bị chặn.
scope_limits: Local/global distinction; no continuation claim without its hypotheses.

statement: Nếu f:R^n→R^n globally Lipschitz thì với mọi initial state, autonomous system x'=f(x) có nghiệm duy nhất tồn tại cho mọi t∈R.
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional vector field defined on all R^n and globally Lipschitz.

statement: Nếu p,q liên tục trên một khoảng I, phương trình y'+p(t)y=q(t) có đúng một nghiệm trên toàn I qua mỗi condition y(t0)=y0 với t0∈I.
scope_limits: First-order scalar linear ODE; coefficient continuity is on the same interval I.

statement: Với autonomous scalar ODE y'=f(y), điểm y* thỏa f(y*)=0 tạo equilibrium solution y(t)≡y*.
scope_limits: Equilibrium specialization; generic zero/function semantics remain earlier ownership.

statement: Khi uniqueness giữ cho autonomous scalar ODE, một non-equilibrium solution không thể đi qua một equilibrium rồi tiếp tục như nghiệm khác, vì solutions gặp cùng state phải trùng trên common continuation domain.
scope_limits: Requires uniqueness; false as a general inference when uniqueness fails.

statement: Trong separable ODE y'=g(t)h(y), chia cho h(y) chỉ hợp lệ nơi h(y)≠0; equilibrium solutions tại zero của h phải được kiểm tra riêng để tránh mất nghiệm.
scope_limits: Separation technique; not every ODE is separable.

statement: Một ODE bậc m đã giải theo đạo hàm cao nhất có thể viết thành hệ bậc nhất bằng cách đưa các đạo hàm thấp hơn vào vector state.
scope_limits: Existence/uniqueness must then be checked on the resulting first-order vector field.

statement: Dưới local-Lipschitz hypotheses phù hợp, solutions tồn tại trên một common compact time interval và ở lại trong một suitable compact region phụ thuộc liên tục vào initial data.
scope_limits: Local continuous dependence; no global/uniform claim outside the common existence region.

statement: Bài toán y'=y^2, y(0)=1 có nghiệm y(t)=1/(1-t), nên một smooth vector field trên R vẫn có thể sinh finite-time blow-up và smoothness alone không bảo đảm global existence.
scope_limits: Counterexample to local smoothness ⇒ global existence.

statement: PDE là quan hệ chứa hàm chưa biết của từ hai independent variables trở lên cùng partial derivatives của nó; bậc là bậc derivative cao nhất thực sự xuất hiện.
scope_limits: PDE definition; multivariable derivative primitives remain C05-owned.

statement: Với second-order linear PDE principal part A u_xx+2B u_xy+C u_yy, dấu B^2-AC phân loại principal part tại điểm là elliptic khi <0, parabolic khi =0, hyperbolic khi >0, nơi principal part không trivial.
scope_limits: Two-variable real principal-part classification; lower-order terms do not determine the label.

statement: Một PDE problem được xác định bởi equation cùng domain và data thích hợp, như initial data hoặc Dirichlet/Neumann boundary data.
scope_limits: Not every combination of data is admissible or well posed.

statement: Initial và boundary data phải thỏa compatibility conditions cần thiết tại nơi chúng gặp nhau nếu yêu cầu classical solution có corresponding regularity.
scope_limits: Compatibility depends on the PDE, domain, and requested regularity class.

statement: Nếu Ω bounded connected và u∈C^2(Ω)∩C(closure Ω) harmonic, maximum và minimum trên closure Ω được controlled by boundary values; an interior strict extremum forces the standard constant-case consequence.
scope_limits: Classical harmonic maximum principle under stated domain/regularity hypotheses.

statement: Nếu u,v∈C^2(Ω)∩C(closure Ω) solve the same Poisson equation on bounded connected Ω and have identical Dirichlet boundary values, thì u=v.
scope_limits: Classical Dirichlet uniqueness via maximum principle for u-v; does not assert existence.

statement: Một formally specified PDE và data không tự bảo đảm classical existence; existence và regularity phụ thuộc type, domain, coefficients, forcing, data và function space.
scope_limits: General solvability caution; no universal existence theorem is being claimed.

statement: Weak solution được đặc trưng bằng integral identity với test functions để chuyển derivatives khỏi solution; weak solvability không tự suy ra classical regularity nếu thiếu regularity theorem.
scope_limits: Bounded weak-solution concept; function-space primitives inherited from C05.

statement: Với κ>0, nếu w∈C^{2,1}(Ω×(0,T])∩C(closure Ω×[0,T]) trên bounded Ω solves w_t-κΔw=0, has zero spatial-boundary data and w(·,0)=0, parabolic maximum principle gives w≡0.
scope_limits: Classical homogeneous heat initial-boundary uniqueness under explicit hypotheses.

statement: Wave equation u_tt-c^2Δu=0, c>0, is hyperbolic; second-order time evolution requires initial displacement and velocity, plus suitable boundary conditions on bounded spatial domains.
scope_limits: Describes data structure; not a solvability assertion for arbitrary data.

statement: For u_t+b(t,x)·∇u=0, if b is regular enough for unique characteristics x'=b(t,x) and u is C^1, u is constant along each characteristic.
scope_limits: Homogeneous transport equation under characteristic uniqueness and C1 regularity.

statement: Characteristic construction for first-order PDE needs appropriate coefficient/data regularity and noncharacteristic initial data when used to build a local classical solution.
scope_limits: Precise hypotheses vary by equation; no blanket characteristic existence claim.

statement: For some nonlinear first-order PDE, characteristics can intersect and a classical single-valued solution can lose smoothness even from smooth initial data.
scope_limits: Shock/gradient-blow-up type phenomenon; weak solution theory may then be needed.

statement: The label elliptic/parabolic/hyperbolic alone does not determine existence, uniqueness, or regularity for a concrete PDE problem.
scope_limits: Solvability also needs domain/coefficient/data/function-space hypotheses.

statement: A discrete dynamical system evolves by x_{n+1}=F(x_n); a continuous flow satisfies φ_0=id and φ_{t+s}=φ_t∘φ_s whenever all terms are defined.
scope_limits: Generic map primitives remain C01/C03; C06 owns temporal evolution semantics.

statement: An autonomous ODE x'=f(x) with locally Lipschitz f generates a local flow by existence-uniqueness; global flow for all t requires global existence of the relevant solutions.
scope_limits: Local versus global flow explicit.

statement: An orbit is the set of states reached by evolution from an initial state; a continuous-time trajectory is the time-parameterized state path.
scope_limits: Phase-space geometry is representation, not the dynamical law.

statement: A set S is forward invariant when every trajectory starting in S remains in S for every forward time for which the evolution is defined.
scope_limits: Full invariance may require backward existence.

statement: For continuous autonomous dynamics, equilibrium x* satisfies f(x*)=0; for a discrete map, fixed point x* satisfies F(x*)=x*.
scope_limits: Special invariant states; generic equation/function semantics inherited.

statement: A nonconstant continuous-time solution is periodic if some T>0 satisfies x(t+T)=x(t) throughout its periodic domain; the least positive such T, when it exists, is its period.
scope_limits: Exact recurrence, not transient oscillation.

statement: A point of map F has period k when F^k(x)=x and k is the least positive integer with that property.
scope_limits: Discrete periodic point; generic composition remains C03-owned.

statement: If a forward orbit exists for all t≥0 and has precompact closure, its omega-limit set consists of limits of x(t_j) along sequences t_j→∞.
scope_limits: Requires a global forward orbit and stated compactness setting.

statement: F and G are topologically conjugate on corresponding invariant sets when a homeomorphism h satisfies h∘F=G∘h; conjugacy carries orbit and period structure between them.
scope_limits: Bounded dynamical use of topology; does not open C09 generic topology.

statement: For an autonomous ODE with uniqueness, two solutions that attain the same phase-space state at the same reference time coincide on their common continuation interval.
scope_limits: Noncrossing consequence requires uniqueness.

statement: A nonautonomous system x'=f(t,x) generally does not define a one-parameter autonomous flow on x alone; it needs a two-time evolution process or an extended state when appropriate.
scope_limits: Autonomous/nonautonomous distinction.

statement: A phase portrait is a representation of orbits/trajectories; a local phase portrait does not by itself prove global existence or global behavior outside the analyzed region.
scope_limits: C04 geometry may represent phase space but supplies no dynamical conclusion.

statement: Equilibrium x* is Lyapunov stable if every ε>0 admits δ>0 such that sufficiently δ-close initial states have forward solutions that remain ε-close to x*.
scope_limits: Local equilibrium stability with forward existence included.

statement: An equilibrium is asymptotically stable when it is Lyapunov stable and attracts all initial states in some neighborhood as t→∞.
scope_limits: Attraction plus stability; attraction alone is not the definition.

statement: Local exponential stability means there are M≥1, α>0 and δ>0 with ||x(t)-x*||≤M e^{-α(t-t0)}||x(t0)-x*|| for sufficiently close initial states over forward time.
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional local exponential stability, assuming the corresponding solutions exist.

statement: Local exponential stability implies local asymptotic stability.
scope_limits: One-way implication; converse generally fails.

statement: For finite-dimensional x'=Ax, if every eigenvalue of A has negative real part, the origin is exponentially stable.
scope_limits: Continuous-time linear system; eigen primitives remain C03-owned.

statement: For x'=Ax, any eigenvalue of A with positive real part makes the origin unstable.
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional linear instability criterion.

statement: For x'=Ax, if every eigenvalue has nonpositive real part and each imaginary-axis eigenvalue is semisimple, the origin is Lyapunov stable.
scope_limits: Semisimplicity is essential on imaginary-axis modes.

statement: A nontrivial Jordan block associated with an imaginary-axis eigenvalue of A produces polynomial growth in e^{At} and makes the origin of x'=Ax not Lyapunov stable.
scope_limits: Explains boundary-spectrum Jordan requirement.

statement: An equilibrium x* of a C^1 vector field is hyperbolic when Jacobian Df(x*) has no eigenvalue with zero real part.
scope_limits: Uses C05 Jacobian and C03 eigen primitives rather than reauthoring them.

statement: If f is C^1 near equilibrium x* and every eigenvalue of Df(x*) has negative real part, then x* is locally exponentially stable.
scope_limits: Nonlinear linearization theorem under explicit C1/spectral hypotheses.

statement: If f is C^1 near equilibrium x* and Df(x*) has an eigenvalue with positive real part, then x* is unstable.
scope_limits: Positive-real-part nonlinear instability criterion.

statement: If Df(x*) has zero-real-part eigenvalues and no positive-real-part eigenvalue, the linear eigenvalue test alone generally does not determine nonlinear stability.
scope_limits: Nonhyperbolic case requires higher-order/nonlinear analysis.

statement: If a C^1 Lyapunov function V is positive definite near an equilibrium and V-dot=∇V·f is nonpositive there, the equilibrium is Lyapunov stable under the standard local domain/sublevel hypotheses.
scope_limits: Lyapunov direct method; local invariant/sublevel control is part of theorem use.

statement: Under the corresponding local Lyapunov hypotheses, positive-definite V with negative-definite V-dot gives local asymptotic stability.
scope_limits: Strict decay is needed for this basic asymptotic conclusion.

statement: For a C^1 discrete map near a fixed point, if every eigenvalue of DF(x*) has modulus <1, the fixed point is locally asymptotically stable.
scope_limits: Discrete linearization stability under C1 local hypotheses.

statement: For a C^1 discrete map near a fixed point, if DF(x*) has an eigenvalue with modulus >1, the fixed point is unstable.
scope_limits: Discrete linearization instability under C1 local hypotheses.

statement: If DF(x*) has eigenvalues on the unit circle and none outside it, eigenvalues alone generally do not determine nonlinear fixed-point stability.
scope_limits: Nonhyperbolic discrete boundary case.

statement: A periodic orbit of an autonomous continuous-time system is the orbit of a nonconstant periodic solution; equilibrium is kept separate as a constant invariant state.
scope_limits: Curriculum terminology excludes equilibrium from periodic-orbit label.

statement: Oscillatory-looking transient behavior such as sign changes or spiraling with changing amplitude does not imply periodicity, because periodicity requires exact repetition after a fixed period.
scope_limits: Transient oscillation versus exact periodicity.

statement: For ω>0, every nonzero solution of x''+ω^2x=0 is periodic with period 2π/ω.
scope_limits: Mathematical oscillator example; physical interpretation is B1.2 boundary.

statement: For ω>0 and 0<ζ<1, nonzero solutions of x''+2ζωx'+ω^2x=0 have oscillatory factors with exponentially decaying amplitude and therefore are not nonzero periodic solutions.
scope_limits: Underdamped mathematical example; no physical ownership.

statement: A scalar autonomous ODE y'=f(y) with unique solutions has no nonconstant periodic solution.
scope_limits: One-dimensional autonomous uniqueness consequence.

statement: A limit cycle is an isolated periodic orbit of a continuous-time dynamical system.
scope_limits: Isolation is among periodic orbits; equilibrium excluded by the curriculum convention.

statement: Orbital asymptotic stability means nearby trajectories approach a periodic orbit as a set, possibly with phase shift, rather than converge to one fixed point on that orbit.
scope_limits: Separates orbital stability from equilibrium point stability.

statement: For a C^1 planar flow, if a positive semi-orbit remains in a compact region and its omega-limit set contains no equilibrium, Poincaré–Bendixson gives that omega-limit set as a periodic orbit.
scope_limits: Planar theorem with compactness and no-equilibrium hypotheses.

statement: A local Poincaré return map is defined on a transverse section near a periodic orbit when flow and section are sufficiently regular; the periodic orbit corresponds to a fixed point of the return map.
scope_limits: Local construction requiring genuine transverse return.

statement: If the relevant transverse derivative/multipliers of the local Poincaré return map lie strictly inside the unit circle, the corresponding periodic orbit is locally orbitally asymptotically stable.
scope_limits: Hyperbolic return-map stability; neutral flow direction is removed by the section.

statement: Existence of oscillation or a periodic orbit does not prove a Hopf bifurcation occurred; Hopf is a mechanism requiring its own spectral, transversality and nondegeneracy hypotheses.
scope_limits: Phenomenon/mechanism distinction across T05/T06.

statement: A bifurcation parameter value is one where qualitative structure of invariant solutions or orbit behavior changes; a numerical change in a coefficient alone is not automatically a bifurcation.
scope_limits: Qualitative-equivalence notion must be specified in theorem use.

statement: If f(x0,μ0)=0, f is sufficiently C^1, and D_x f(x0,μ0) is invertible, implicit-function theorem gives a unique local equilibrium branch x(μ) near (x0,μ0).
scope_limits: Finite-dimensional local continuation; consumes accepted C05 implicit-function primitive.

statement: Because invertible D_x f gives unique local equilibrium continuation, a local change in equilibrium count at a candidate point requires singular D_x f there.
scope_limits: Necessary, not sufficient, condition for local equilibrium-count bifurcation.

statement: For scalar x'=f(x,μ), if f=0, f_x=0, f_xx≠0 and f_μ≠0 at the critical point with suitable smoothness, saddle-node theorem gives a local fold with two equilibria on one parameter side and none on the other.
scope_limits: Generic one-dimensional saddle-node hypotheses and local conclusion.

statement: The normal form x'=μx-x^2 has equilibrium branches x=0 and x=μ that exchange stability at μ=0, illustrating transcritical bifurcation.
scope_limits: Canonical example, not a generic theorem without additional nondegeneracy hypotheses.

statement: The normal form x'=μx-x^3 shows symmetric pitchfork structure, but a generic pitchfork conclusion requires symmetry or corresponding structural conditions; symmetry-breaking perturbations can unfold it.
scope_limits: Pitchfork is not generic in unrestricted one-parameter families.

statement: Hopf bifurcation requires an equilibrium branch with exactly one simple complex-conjugate eigenvalue pair on the imaginary axis at nonzero frequency and no other imaginary-axis eigenvalues.
scope_limits: Spectral hypotheses only; crossing/nondegeneracy are separate required claims.

statement: Generic Hopf conclusion additionally requires transverse crossing of the critical pair through the imaginary axis and nonzero first Lyapunov coefficient, yielding a local branch of small periodic orbits.
scope_limits: Transversality and nondegeneracy explicit; local theorem only.

statement: Observing a purely imaginary eigenvalue pair at one parameter value is insufficient to conclude Hopf bifurcation.
scope_limits: Missing crossing or nondegeneracy can prevent Hopf.

statement: Hopf criticality and stability of the bifurcating periodic branch depend on normal-form/nondegeneracy data, not only on eigenvalues touching the imaginary axis.
scope_limits: Concrete sign interpretation requires a fixed normal-form convention.

statement: For discrete maps, generic period-doubling requires a multiplier crossing -1 transversely together with standard nondegeneracy conditions; multiplier -1 at one point alone is insufficient.
scope_limits: Local flip-bifurcation theorem hypotheses.

statement: Normal-form and local bifurcation conclusions control only a neighborhood of the critical state and parameter and do not determine global dynamics far away.
scope_limits: Local/global boundary explicit.

statement: Existence of an equilibrium or periodic branch after bifurcation does not determine its stability; stability requires a separate valid criterion such as linearization, return-map or Lyapunov analysis.
scope_limits: Existence-versus-stability distinction using only opened primitives.

statement: Deterministic chaos is complex aperiodic behavior generated by a deterministic evolution law; determinism does not mean probabilistic randomness.
scope_limits: Probability/statistics C07 is locked and supplies no support.

statement: For continuous map F on invariant metric set X, sensitive dependence can mean there exists δ>0 such that every x and every neighborhood of x contains y and an iterate n with d(F^n(x),F^n(y))>δ.
scope_limits: Map-based sensitivity definition; continuous-time variants require their own formulation.

statement: A Devaney-style chaos definition for a continuous map on an invariant metric space combines topological transitivity, dense periodic points and sensitive dependence.
scope_limits: One standard curriculum convention; other definitions exist.

statement: Different chaos definitions in the literature are not always equivalent without additional hypotheses on state space and map.
scope_limits: Prevents treating one diagnostic as a universal definition.

statement: For a differentiable map, an upper Lyapunov exponent along an orbit/direction may be expressed as a limsup logarithmic growth rate of ||DF^n(x)v||; a positive value indicates exponential linearized separation along that orbit/direction.
scope_limits: Directional/orbit diagnostic; derivative primitive inherited from C05.

statement: A positive finite-time or numerically estimated Lyapunov-style value alone does not prove Devaney chaos or universal chaos of the whole system.
scope_limits: Finite-time/asymptotic and local/global distinctions; numerical methods C10 remain locked.

statement: A chaotic invariant set need not be an attractor; an attractor additionally attracts a neighborhood under the definition being used.
scope_limits: Chaos-versus-attraction distinction; attractor definitions can vary.

statement: The logistic family F_r(x)=r x(1-x) is deterministic and its behavior depends on r; not every parameter value r is chaotic.
scope_limits: Canonical one-dimensional family; no probability claim.

statement: A parameter family can contain periodic windows interspersed with chaotic regimes, so chaos cannot be generalized from one chaotic parameter to all parameters.
scope_limits: Parameter-local statement.

statement: Topological conjugacy on invariant sets preserves orbit correspondence, periodicity and transitivity-type structure, so qualitative chaos structure is not merely a coordinate-label artifact.
scope_limits: Metric sensitivity can require care under nonuniform metric changes.

statement: Poincaré–Bendixson constrains omega-limit behavior for bounded C^1 planar flows under its hypotheses, so an oscillatory-looking planar phase portrait alone is not evidence of chaos.
scope_limits: Planar-flow constraint; does not exclude higher-dimensional/map chaos.

statement: A time-evolving mathematical model should specify state variables, time domain, parameters/inputs, evolution law, required initial/boundary data and relevant outputs/observables.
scope_limits: Model specification discipline; domain-specific semantics remain later science ownership.

statement: Predictions from a model are conditional on its stated structural assumptions, parameter choices and data assumptions.
scope_limits: Mathematical conditionality; empirical truth is not implied.

statement: Autonomous continuous-time state evolution may be written x'=f(x), nonautonomous evolution x'=f(t,x), and discrete time-varying evolution x_{n+1}=F(n,x_n).
scope_limits: Distinct evolution forms; generic function notation inherited.

statement: A nonautonomous ODE x'=f(t,x) can be embedded as τ'=1, x'=f(τ,x) when regularity/domain allow, with time added as a state coordinate.
scope_limits: Mathematical reformulation changes the state space.

statement: A deterministic IVP model is well posed in a specified class only when existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence are all established; these properties are not interchangeable.
scope_limits: Exact topology/function class must be specified in concrete use.

statement: If I is C^1 and x'=f(x) autonomous, condition ∇I(x)·f(x)=0 on the domain makes I(x(t)) constant along every solution while it exists.
scope_limits: Conserved quantity via accepted C05 chain rule; no physical conservation ownership.

statement: Linear model near equilibrium x* uses Df(x*) only as a local first-order approximation when f is differentiable; stability inference still needs T04 linearization hypotheses.
scope_limits: Consumes C05 derivative and C06-T04 stability; no unconditional spectral inference.

statement: Time-dependent coefficients or inputs can destroy equilibrium/invariant structures present in an autonomous version, so actual structure must be checked from the time-varying evolution law.
scope_limits: General modeling caution; no physical-domain claim.

statement: Parameter estimation, statistical uncertainty analysis and numerical simulation are additional tasks beyond merely specifying an evolution law; the dynamical equation alone does not supply their results.
scope_limits: In HKA, C07 probability/statistics and C10 numerical/optimization remain locked; no locked Claim IDs are used.

statement: Solving a model equation exactly establishes mathematical consequences of its assumptions but does not by itself establish empirical adequacy of the model.
scope_limits: Mathematical solution versus empirical validation.

statement: Empirical validation requires comparison of model outputs with relevant observations/data and assessment of a domain of validity; that conclusion belongs application/domain-science stages when opened.
scope_limits: Boundary-only validation discipline; B1.2 and later sciences are not current support.
